concepts.preferred_label: Dextrocardia with complete right bundle branch block
concepts.why: The patient's physical examination and echocardiogram results show the apex of the heart located on the right side of the chest, and the right atrium and ventricle are on the left side, indicating dextrocardia, and the ECG findings demonstrate a complete right bundle branch block.
The ECG findings demonstrate a wide complex rhythm with right bundle branch block morphology and a QRS duration of 120 milliseconds, indicating a right bundle branch block.

The patient's physical examination and echocardiogram results show the apex of the heart located on the right side of the chest, and the liver is located in the left subcostal region, indicating situs inversus.
The patient's echocardiogram results show the right atrium and ventricle on the left side, and the left atrium and ventricle on the right side, indicating cardiac malposition.
The patient's physical examination and echocardiogram results show abnormalities in the heart's structure and position, indicating a congenital heart defect.
The ECG findings demonstrate a wide complex rhythm and negative P waves, indicating an arrhythmia.
The ECG findings demonstrate a wide complex rhythm and a QRS duration of 120 milliseconds, indicating a cardiac conduction abnormality.
The ECG findings demonstrate positive P waves in lead V1 and biphasic P waves in leads V2 through V6, indicating right atrial enlargement.
The pathological Q waves in leads V5 and V6 are indicative of a previous myocardial infarction.
